t: You're on St Martin's Le Grand, a street in the City of London, north of Newgate Street and Cheapside and south of Aldersgate Street. It's the southernmost stretch of the A1. The name was once used as shorthand for the postal authorities, much as Scotland Yard stands for the police, because the General Post Office had its headquarters here from 1829 to 1984. The area was formerly a liberty within the City. William Wigan, a landowner in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, in the late seventeenth century, is recorded as having lived here.
